- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–2% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% below true peak for next 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in early forecast horizon (1–7 days); apply slight upward bias if sentiment is positive, downward if negative.
- For 14–30 day forecasts, model underestimates upward momentum; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment is positive and price has been trending up.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift within 3–5 days.
- Avoid overfitting to recent low prices; if sentiment is positive but price is stuck near low, model may underestimate recovery; add 1–2% to forecast for next 5 days.
